description: macOS user-level caches, logs, device backups and other system leftovers.

rules.name: Mail attachment copies
rules.reason: Copies of attachments you opened from Mail. The originals stay in your mailbox.
rules.regenerates: Mail re-creates them when you open an attachment again.

rules.name: Downloaded iPhone/iPad updates
rules.reason: iOS/iPadOS firmware files downloaded by Finder/iTunes to update a device.
rules.regenerates: Downloaded again if you ever update or restore a device from this Mac.

rules.name: iPhone/iPad backup
rules.reason: A local backup of an iPhone or iPad. Old backups of devices you no longer own are pure waste; your current device's latest backup may be worth keeping.

rules.name: App logs
rules.reason: Diagnostic logs written by apps. Only useful when debugging a problem.
rules.regenerates: Apps write new logs as they run.

rules.name: App cache
rules.reason: Cache files an app keeps to speed itself up. Contains no documents or settings.
rules.regenerates: The app rebuilds it as needed (it may feel a little slower the first time).

rules.name: macOS installer app
rules.reason: A full macOS installer (often 12+ GB) left over after an upgrade.
rules.advice: Apple-signed, so disksweep won't move it. If you don't need it, drag it to the Trash in Finder.

rules.name: Items already in the Trash
rules.reason: Files in the Trash still use disk space until it is emptied.
rules.advice: Use the empty_old_trash tool (lists first, asks before deleting) or empty the Trash in Finder.
